Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract in `README.md`, then inspect the required control bookshelf and both rollout visual views before proposing or editing the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and verify that exactly one candidate plus both required documentation updates are present.

The inherited guidance shows a mature controller lineage: the best measured mechanism is coherent transit with posterior-priority allocation, while recent work has focused on terminal allocation and has repeatedly failed when adding shared yaw/course feedback. I’m now comparing the prefilled parent against the strongest and most informative sampled alternatives, including both keyframe rows and actuator/trajectory diagnostics, before choosing a genuinely new mechanism.

The `fish-control-primitives` consultation is now timely: three sampled descendants introduced different load/allocation selectors, yet all remained in the same capture class and none beat the v20 parent’s mean-distance/score. I’ll use the shelf only to identify a new invariant that fits the measured terminal defect—not to tune gains or import published kinematics.

The decisive evidence is not a new route error: the parent reaches capture fastest among the four samples, but arrives with `0.1092` course alignment, `0.984 rad/T` yaw, and `0.8767U` target-normal speed. In its near-approach samples, summed joint rate correlates `0.415` with target-normal force; when tail motion shares the slip sign, target-normal speed rises over the next `0.022T`, while the opposite half-cycle reduces it. I’ll test that phase distinction directly with bounded, approach-only posterior feathering.

The pre-edit note is now in place. The single candidate change will be narrowly scoped: retain the parent’s route, cadence, lag, mean-bend conservation, and actuator governor, while replacing only the raw yaw-power envelope selector with the trace-supported slip/half-cycle selector.

The candidate and durable guidance lesson are both updated. The new guidance records the three sampled force-power placement failures and narrows the next reusable test to immediate joint-state phase. I’m invoking the mandated checker now, while also running local schema, boundary, symmetry, and activation checks; no CFD will be run.

The mandated checker was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’m following the checker’s immutable contract directly from its configuration and will repair and rerun every available check; the checker invocation failure itself does not authorize skipping validation.

All available checks now pass: guidance materiality, solver boundary, parameter schema, reflection invariance, exact pre-approach inactivity, and preservation of the opposite half-cycle. I’m doing one final provenance/readability pass and rerunning the guidance guard after the last numeric correction.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8).

The v26 policy adds approach-only, reflection-invariant posterior half-cycle feathering based on target-normal velocity and summed joint rate. Far/middle behavior remains unchanged.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:188)

Guidance materiality, solver boundary, schema, reflection, inactivity, and half-cycle authority checks pass. The mandated checker was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable; its checks were run directly. Julia was unavailable, so no executable smoke test ran. No CFD was run.
